skill.name: golang-modernize
skill.description: Guides version-aware Go modernization using recent language features, standard library APIs, testing patterns, and tooling checks while preserving project compatibility.
skill.summary: Review and modernize Go code with version-aware, testable recommendations.
skill.author: samber

security_audit.summary: All 118 static findings are false positives caused by Markdown backticks, JSON evaluation fixtures, ordinary Go examples, and documentation URLs. content.user_title: Modernize Go Code with Current Idioms
content.value_statement: Older Go patterns can limit safety, clarity, and maintainability. This skill recommends version-compatible language, library, testing, and tooling improvements.
actual_capabilities: Reads go.mod or go.work to identify the project target version.
Finds compatible language, standard library, testing, and deprecated API improvements.
Prioritizes safety and correctness before readability and gradual cleanup.
Guides migrations for Go versions 1.21 through 1.27.
Uses Go tests and modernization tools to validate proposed changes.
Records explicitly declined suggestions in a project .modernize file.
limitations: Coverage focuses on Go 1.21 through 1.27 and is narrower for older projects.
It does not perform structural refactoring, function extraction, or package moves.
Tool checks require installed Go tooling and may access configured module sources.
Dependency and version upgrades still require project-specific compatibility review.

use_cases.title: Upgrade a Maintained Service
use_cases.description: Review an existing service before raising its Go directive and identify required compatibility checks.

use_cases.title: Reduce Legacy Patterns
use_cases.description: Replace outdated APIs and verbose patterns with compatible standard library features.

use_cases.title: Refresh CI Tooling
use_cases.description: Add modernization linting, vulnerability checks, tests, and repeatable upgrade validation.

prompt_templates.title: Review One File
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this Go file for modernizations compatible with the current go.mod version. Explain each recommendation before editing.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review of a focused file

prompt_templates.title: Modernize a Package
prompt_templates.prompt: Modernize this Go package using compatible language and standard library features. Run focused tests and summarize behavior changes.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Version Upgrade
prompt_templates.prompt: Assess upgrading this module to Go 1.27. Identify breaking changes, dependency concerns, migration steps, and required validation.

prompt_templates.title: Audit the Repository
prompt_templates.prompt: Perform a repository-wide modernization audit. Prioritize correctness, deprecated APIs, testing, tooling, and low-risk changes with validation evidence.

output_examples.input: Review this Go 1.22 package for modernization opportunities.
output: High priority: remove obsolete loop variable shadow copies and verify concurrent tests.
Medium priority: replace manual helpers with compatible slices, maps, min, and max APIs.
Validation: run focused tests, then the complete package test suite.

output_examples.input: Prepare this service for a Go 1.27 upgrade.
output: Check removed GODEBUG settings and JSON decoding behavior before changing the module directive.
Review deprecated dependencies and confirm replacement feature parity.
Run module cleanup, tests, linting, and vulnerability checks after approved edits.

output_examples.input: Modernize our Go testing and CI setup.
output: Use deterministic testing APIs where the target version supports them.
Add modernization linting and vulnerability scanning to CI.
Keep broad repository changes isolated until maintainers review the results.

best_practices: Confirm the module target version before recommending newer APIs.
Prioritize correctness and security changes, then readability and gradual cleanup.
Run focused and complete tests after each approved modernization group.
anti_patterns: Do not recommend APIs newer than the module target without an approved version upgrade.
Do not mix unrelated structural refactoring into a modernization change.
Do not remove dependencies before checking behavior, release notes, and transitive usage.

faq.question: Which Go versions receive detailed coverage?
faq.answer: The bundled guidance focuses on Go 1.21 through Go 1.27, with selected older baseline improvements.

faq.question: Does the skill edit code automatically?
faq.answer: It can apply approved changes, but broad scans should be reviewed before repository-wide edits.

faq.question: Can it upgrade go.mod?
faq.answer: Yes, after assessing compatibility and receiving approval for the target Go version.

faq.question: Does it replace structural refactoring help?
faq.answer: No. Function extraction, package moves, and architecture changes remain outside this skill.

faq.question: Which validation tools can it use?
faq.answer: It can use Go tests, golangci-lint modernization checks, go fix, module cleanup, and govulncheck when available.

faq.question: How are declined recommendations handled?
faq.answer: The skill can record explicit declines in .modernize so they are not repeated during the session.
